radiology_report:
Radiology Service | OLVG Amsterdam | 15 January 2025
Study: Multiparametric MRI of the Prostate

Clinical Context:
70-year-old male evaluated for prostate malignancy after a PSA reading of 8.8 ng/mL.

Observations:
The gland measures 33.02 mL in total volume. T2 sequences highlight a discrete region of intermediate signal intensity within the right posterior peripheral zone at the mid-gland, spanning roughly 8 by 6 mm. Apparent diffusion coefficient maps confirm restricted diffusion. Post-contrast kinetics lack focal early enhancement. Seminal vesicles appear intact. No extraprostatic extension or suspicious pelvic lymph nodes are visible. The bladder and rectal walls maintain normal morphology.

Summary:
PI-RADS 3 lesion located in the right posterior peripheral zone at mid-gland. Prostate volume 33.02 mL, yielding a PSA density of 0.267 ng/mL/mL. csPCa predicted probability 0.7255827.

previous_notes.author: Dr. K. Bakker (GP)
previous_notes.text: A standard screening visit documented a prostate-specific antigen level of 4.5 ng/mL. The individual reports no symptoms, maintaining controlled blood pressure and consistent kidney function parameters.

previous_notes.author: Dr. K. Bakker (GP)
previous_notes.text: Subsequent laboratory testing indicated a PSA increase to 6.9 ng/mL during July 2024, contrasting with an earlier value of 5.3 ng/mL. Monitoring the progressive trend alongside the patient's age prompted a transfer to the urology department for comprehensive imaging and clinical evaluation.
